about: Regions for tools/xdk_sigmatch/region_compare.py: the lighting validation of the native renderer (spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-07-native-renderer-lighting-design.md, success criteria 4 to 6) at the three daylight spots of the -BootSave Hero000 plans.
coordinates: rect = [x0, y0, x1, y1] as fractions of the client area (0, 0 top left). Chosen on 1942 x 1136 window shots (client area 1920 x 1080 at 11, 45).

kinds.sunlit: in the sun in the emulated shots: counts for criterion 4 (native mean luminance within 25% of the emulated one, hue within 10 degrees, after calibrating on 'dirt patch' at the bridge)
kinds.averted: the side of an object turned from the sun; used by a pair (criterion 5), not counted for criterion 4
kinds.shadowed: in a cast shadow in the emulated shots (criterion 6): the native picture has no shadows, so the region is expected too bright and is listed, not counted
kinds.haze: far ground behind the game's haze, which the native picture does not draw (spec: fog and haze are out of scope): expected darker and less blue, listed, not counted
kinds.provisional: tree leaves: not lit when the regions were chosen (Task 8c); to be confirmed on shots of the build that lights them

chosen_on: out/native-evidence/lighting/task8b_<spot>_shot_<t>s.png of 2026-10-08 (binary of commit 9803971): bridge 36 s emulated, 40 s native, 44 s emulated; third 44, 48, 52; trees 58, 62, 66. A run with another camera position needs the rectangles checked again (the third spot's walk ends slightly elsewhere from run to run).

regions.name: grass beside it

CORRECTED in plan Task 9: the first rectangle, [0.215, 0.515, 0.285, 0.545], straddled the edge of a moving leaf shadow (its left half is dark in the emulated shots and changes by -51% to +57% between 36 s and 44 s; out/native-evidence/lighting/task9/grass_pole_341.txt). The shaded part is the next region; this rectangle was chosen once, from the picture, before its ratio was computed

Stands before the bright haze over the far hills: the emulated picture's blur mixes about a sixth of that background into the thin pole (plan Task 9, grass_pole_341.txt), so the ratio and the hue here measure the missing post chain as well as the light; the pair is what the pole is for
